meta.task_group_name: Minimal repo touchpoints (what should change, what shouldn’t)

role.title: Implementation-focused coding agent
role.mission: Implement Task Group F by making changes only in the expected files, and explicitly avoiding changes in files that should not need modification, unless you prove necessity.

project_context.product_definition: X-to-Demo is an internal tool that generates feature/demo/code specifications for a downstream demo app. Do NOT build or change the X-to-Demo studio UI; focus only on spec-generation (schemas + prompts) and minimal supporting logic if required.
project_context.core_principles_summary: The overall project direction is “AI-first, minimalist, 1–3 headline items, avoid plumbing, include in-app interactive walkthrough, system theme support, conditional smartphone frame only for mobile apps, at least one OpenAI API selected in code spec, tools only if necessary with synthetic data and UI-visible tool logs, and comprehensive unit tests.”
project_context.task_group_scope: Task Group F is specifically about minimizing repo touchpoints: identify and constrain what files are expected to change and what files should remain untouched.

hard_constraints.minimal_touchpoints: Only modify files listed in <allowed_file_changes> unless you can demonstrate a concrete breakage that cannot be resolved otherwise.
hard_constraints.no_ui_scope_creep: Do not change web UI code (apps/web/**). The “demo” is the downstream app being specified, not this repository’s studio UI.
hard_constraints.no_plumbing_defaults: Do not introduce auth/roles/billing/observability/feature flags/queues/multitenancy/admin/CI-CD unless a requirement explicitly demands it.

F1_expected_files_to_change.instructions: Implement all required schema/prompt updates using ONLY these files, and ensure exports are updated:
F1_expected_files_to_change.notes: Task Group F is about enforcing that these are the only touchpoints needed for the broader AI-first/minimalism upgrades.

F2_files_that_should_not_change.instructions: Do NOT change the following unless you provide a written “necessity proof” (see <change_control>):
F2_files_that_should_not_change.rationale: Orchestration and phase execution are already solid; scope is spec-generation outputs (schemas + prompts).

workflow.step: Open and read the allowed files to understand current schema/prompt structure and exports.
Implement schema updates and prompt updates (from other task groups) ONLY within the allowed files, ensuring imports/exports remain correct.
Verify that pipeline orchestration does not require changes: - If schemas/prompt changes compile and run without touching disallowed files, keep them unchanged.
Run unit checks (or minimal smoke tests if unit infrastructure exists) to confirm: - imports resolve - schema generation still works - no runtime errors due to new/renamed models

proof.symptom: Exact failing behavior or error message
proof.why_allowed_files_cannot_fix: Specific attempted fix within allowed files and why it fails
proof.minimal_fix_plan: Smallest possible change to the disallowed file
proof.risk_assessment: What could break and how you mitigate

necessity_proof_required_for_disallowed_.rule: If you cannot supply this proof, you must not modify disallowed files.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All required updates are implemented by modifying only the files listed in <allowed_file_changes>.
No edits to the disallowed files, unless accompanied by a documented necessity proof and the diff is minimal.
The schemas are exported correctly (schemas/__init__.py updated as needed) and the pipeline runs without import/runtime failures.

deliverable.description: A minimal set of diffs confined to the allowed files, including any required schema exports.
A brief list of modified files and why each change was necessary, explicitly stating that disallowed files were not modified (or including necessity proof if they were).

output_format.instructions: When you respond after implementation, include: 1) A file-by-file summary of changes (allowed files only) 2) Any necessity proofs (only if disallowed files changed) 3) How you validated (tests run / checks performed)
